parsedVerdict.reasoning:
Most of CancelOrderUseCase.execute is proper application-layer work. It loads the order through a repository port and relies on the domain's order.isCancellable() check. It then releases stock on each product, calls order.cancel() and saves the order. That is use-case coordination, and the business rules stay in domain objects.

One statement does not belong here. execute takes an `any`-typed orderId and runs `Array.isArray(orderId) ? orderId[0] : orderId`. Express route and query values can be `string | string[]`, so this unwraps HTTP request parameters. That is transport input parsing. It belongs in the infrastructure layer, in OrderController (which constructor-injects this use case). The use case should take a typed order ID instead. Because a transport concern has leaked into the application layer, the unit fails. The leak is small, so confidence is moderate.
